headline: Reliable adaptation from imperfect, endogenous feedback.
question: How can imperfect human, evaluator, and environment feedback become learning signals that let AI agents adapt without becoming less reliable?
profile: I am Baixin Guo (Max), an independent researcher with a background in Applied Psychology. I study what feedback actually measures, how persistent state and rules are enforced across different paths, and whether adaptation on seen signals transfers to unseen situations. I design evaluations, inspect failure attribution, and build reproducible research tools.
interests: Human and evaluator feedback; preference learning; human-agent collaboration; reliable adaptation; reproducible AI evaluation.

selectedResearch.title: What the Score Measured
selectedResearch.subtitle: Failure attribution in an agent memory evaluation
selectedResearch.status: Joint public preprint + my methods report · with Dino Vitale, Boundary Labs
selectedResearch.question: When a memory-evaluation task fails, does the outcome score tell us which component failed?
selectedResearch.contribution: Co-designed an observability map that separates outcomes, available evidence, failure attribution, and judge confidence; authored the companion methods report (rubric, test matrix, judging protocol) as its own deposit, and co-authored the public preprint.
selectedResearch.result: Outcome scores alone cannot identify the failing component when traces are missing.
selectedResearch.scope: LongMemEval-based evaluation; claims are bounded to inspected and collaborator-reported evidence.

selectedResearch.title: Preference Modeling Diagnostics
selectedResearch.subtitle: Known-user preference adaptation with identity controls
selectedResearch.question: Does a known user's expressed preference improve predictions on prompts they have never seen?
selectedResearch.contribution: Designed prompt-disjoint evaluation and identity controls to separate stable individual preference signal from leakage.
selectedResearch.result: Regularized adaptation reduced equal-user negative log-likelihood by 0.879% on held-out prompts; wrong-user and shuffled-identity controls removed the advantage.
selectedResearch.scope: CPU-only study across 94 eligible known users; results apply to the tested prompt distribution.

selectedResearch.title: Cross-Consumer Authority Enforcement
selectedResearch.subtitle: One decision, multiple consumer paths
selectedResearch.status: Research note v0.1.1 · bounded single-substrate case study
selectedResearch.question: When one canonical authority decision governs persistent state, do all consumer paths enforce it the same way?
selectedResearch.contribution: Consolidated existing frozen experimental and system evidence into a public research note; identified cross-consumer enforcement divergence in the audited substrate.
selectedResearch.result: In one audited substrate, the same authority decision was applied differently by heterogeneous behavioral consumers.
selectedResearch.scope: Single audited substrate; the note reports no new experiments and makes no cross-system claim.

engineeringContributions.title: W&B rai-toolkit judge prompt data boundary
engineeringContributions.summary: Merged fix that keeps trusted grading rules and the text being scored in separate halves of every LLM-judge prompt: rule prose stays in the system message, row values travel as one structured JSON message, and a scorer whose rule text is missing now stops with an error instead of scoring without rules. Covers 12 scorers with 73 new offline test cases; it narrows where scored text can read as an instruction, and does not claim prompt injection is solved.

collaborations.title: Implicit human feedback
collaborations.context: Research collaboration with Haw-Shiuan Chang, University of Arizona
collaborations.status: Ongoing collaboration · no denoising or prediction gain shown yet
collaborations.summary: Before gaze and mouse logs can serve as implicit feedback, what does the collection mechanism actually let us infer about behavior?
bullets: Audited missing and duplicate events, coordinate validity, temporal gaps and query-trajectory-response alignment, and compared word-run with fixation-proxy representations; this round each drafted summary was tied back to its four coordinates at once — timestamp, word position, the exact displayed-text version that position indexes into, and interface region — so a claim cannot cite a word number taken from a different rendering of the same screen.

Re-checked those summaries with a second, independent implementation rather than the code that produced them: 361 machine-checkable statements, all of which hold, with every quoted timestamp landing on the 0.5-second bin grid and every cited word index falling inside its own text.

collaborations.title: Memory-agent evaluation reliability
collaborations.context: Research collaboration with Dino Vitale, Boundary Labs
collaborations.status: Delivered evaluation framework · two public Zenodo deposits
collaborations.summary: For LongMemEval-based evaluation, I designed a framework that separates observed outcomes, available evidence, failure attribution, and judge confidence. Missing traces limit what a failed answer can tell us about the memory system.
bullets: Delivered an observability map, failure-attribution framework, five diagnostic tests, and a judge-reliability protocol.
Distinguished independently inspected traces from collaborator-reported checks; limited attribution claims to the evidence actually available.
Co-authored the public preprint "What the Score Measured: Failure Attribution in an Agent Memory Evaluation" (Zenodo, October 1, 2026): https://zenodo.org/records/22980060

The methods half is now a deposit of its own — "Failure Attribution and Evaluation Reliability Framework for LongMemEval" (Zenodo v2.0 RC3, October 11, 2026), sole-authored and registered as the supplement to that preprint, so the two records share one research background instead of reading as separate studies: https://zenodo.org/records/23273896

Division of labour as stated by the joint preprint: the source reconstruction, the harness repair, the rerun and the write-up are Dino Vitale's; the audit of public materials, the attribution rubric, the test matrix and the judging protocol are mine.

The judging protocol was applied to 150 predictions, which are 25 cases scored under six conditions — not 150 distinct questions. Both records are Zenodo deposits: neither is peer reviewed, and no submission or acceptance is claimed.

projects.title: Cross-Consumer Authority Enforcement
projects.status: Research note v0.1.1 · bounded single-substrate case study
projects.summary: In one audited persistent-agent substrate, the same canonical authority decision over the same governed state was enforced inconsistently across heterogeneous behavioral consumer paths. I consolidated the existing frozen experimental and system evidence (v0.1-v0.4, consumer-consistency audit, independent adversarial review, cross-substrate replication package) into a public research note; the note reports no new experiments, and this website update added none. Claims are limited to the recorded frozen evidence.
bullets: Consolidated frozen artifacts (v0.1-v0.4, consumer-consistency audit, independent adversarial review, novelty/overlap audit) into public research note v0.1.1.
Scope is one substrate and recorded evidence: no fresh replication, no residual-authority or prompt-injection result, and no claim about whether the underlying authorization was warranted.

projects.title: Preference Modeling Diagnostics
projects.summary: A CPU-only study of whether individual preference signal predicts choices on unseen prompts. Regularized known-user adaptation reduced equal-user negative log-likelihood by 0.879%; wrong-user and shuffled-identity controls removed the advantage.
bullets: Designed prompt-disjoint evaluation and identity controls to distinguish stable individual preference signal from leakage.
Regularized adaptation reduced equal-user negative log-likelihood by 0.879% across 94 eligible known users. Kept the confirmatory test separate from exploratory history-length analysis.

projects.title: Evaluation Runtime
projects.status: Public research prototype · deterministic mock agent
projects.summary: An evaluation runtime that keeps execution attempts, judgments, ambiguous failures, and report denominators separately inspectable. Its public snapshot provides reproducible engineering evidence, with no real-provider reliability validation.
bullets: Specified and co-designed attempt identity, evaluator-version binding, ambiguity-aware recovery, and denominator-aware reports.
Directed implementation and reviewed reproducibility checks. The public snapshot uses deterministic mocks; software checks do not establish real-provider reliability.

projects.title: CheckMyCoach
projects.summary: A human-centered verification prototype that routes selected AI outputs, proposes revisions, and checks both target removal and information retention. Human evaluation has not yet been conducted.
bullets: Co-designed the evaluation decomposition, specified routing and revision behavior, and reviewed outputs against explicit preservation requirements.

In a fixed 40-case constructed development run, 15 cases were routed and 12 delivered outputs removed the target feature; none passed every target-and-retention check. No human-outcome improvement is claimed.

additional.title: OptiFrontier
additional.summary: A prespecified trainability experiment on a GPT-style model, with source, configurations, logs, and a decision record packaged for reproduction. The conclusion is limited to the tested one-seed configuration.
bullets: Ran a prespecified 6,000-step optimizer comparison on a 162M-parameter GPT-style model with a fixed architecture on an A100 GPU.
Documented a trainability gap within that one-seed configuration and packaged commands, logs, hashes, and a bounded decision record.

social_research.title: 谁每天花在劳动上的时间更长？
social_research.status: Interactive research feature · five acts · audited public data
social_research.summary: 用 2024 年全国时间利用调查的公开汇总表，展示「什么被算作劳动」这一统计定义如何改变性别劳动时间比较的结论方向：有酬劳动女−男 −73.9 分钟/天，计入无酬劳动后两类劳动合计 +25.9 分钟/天。
bullets: 读者自己切换统计口径，看到排序反转，并读出它的算术由来（参与率 × 参与者时长与对称恒等式）。
三个心理学与社会学视角作为待检验假说呈现，页面明确标出本调查未测量的构念；不做因果解释。
数据、公式、来源链、复现脚本与公开研究稿随页面一并发布，全部数值由冻结的审计输入派生。
